definitions.explanation: Additional news or information that follows an initial report on the same topic. Common in journalism and news media.

examples.japanese: {続報|ぞくほう}が{入|はい}り{次第|しだい}お{伝|つた}えします。
examples.english: We will report as soon as further news comes in.

examples.japanese: {事件|じけん}の{続報|ぞくほう}を{待|ま}っている。
examples.english: I'm waiting for a follow-up report on the incident.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{被害|ひがい}について{続報|ぞくほう}が{発表|はっぴょう}された。
examples.english: A follow-up report on the typhoon damage was released.

notes:
USAGE:
A news and media term. The phrase {続報|ぞくほう}が{入|はい}り{次第|しだい} (as soon as further news comes in) is a standard journalistic expression heard on TV news and in online reporting.

WORD FORMATION:
{続|ぞく} (continue, follow) + {報|ほう} (report, news).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {速報|そくほう}: breaking news, flash report
- {第一報|だいいっぽう}: first report, initial news
- {詳報|しょうほう}: detailed report

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {続報|ぞくほう}が{入|はい}る: further news comes in
- {続報|ぞくほう}を{待|ま}つ: wait for an update
- {続報|ぞくほう}が{入|はい}り{次第|しだい}: as soon as there is an update
